correctness.rationale: For a≠0 normalize H=t³+bt. The highest possible degree is 9, 6 or 3, and b is recovered respectively from f7/(3f9), f4/(2f6), or the ratio of the t and t³ coefficients of F itself. The remaining fiber coordinates are uniquely obtained in the independent basis H,H²,H³. For a=0 the fiber maps linearly and isomorphically onto P⟨t,t²,t³⟩. These charts overlap in image exactly on L minus [t]; the projective bundle gives a proper birational morphism with finite fibers, hence the finite normalization. The degree also follows from c1(O(1))³=1+2+3 on the bundle of lines. On the a=1 chart order the six columns as t,H,tH,H²,tH²,H³: the distinct highest degrees 1,3,4,6,7,9 give a triangular unit minor (the permutation to the record's order is even). On b=1,a=0, the varying-base column modulo the fiber is 2c₂t⁴+3c₃t⁵, which vanishes only over [t]; two fiber directions always survive. Off L, the sole preimage and injective tangent map imply m_B=m_AB by Nakayama; B=A+m_AB and finiteness imply B/A=0. On L a double fiber or the exceptional rank drop precludes smoothness. Finite properness isolates the two analytic germs at each double-fiber point, and each is a smooth embedded germ by immersion. Their vector tangents share exactly ⟨t,t³⟩ because the determinant with the four additional columns t²,t⁵,F²,F³ has factor α⁵, from the leading terms in degrees 6 and 9. On the [t] chart the inverse image is λ=aμ=0 and the two globally described P¹s meet there and nowhere else.
